The market widely expects Apple to launch a new iPad mini equipped with an OLED screen later this month. An unconfirmed new rumour has again claimed today that the new iPad mini will switch to an OLED display, but will still only have a 60Hz refresh rate and will not support ProMotion.

The OLED version of the iPad mini may lack ProMotion

This is already the second time we have heard this rumour, but both times it comes from the same source: the yeux1122 account on the Naver website. That account has a mixed track record when it comes to Apple rumours, and often appears to simply relay information from anonymous sources rather than offering any exclusive insights.

However, yeux1122's latest post claims that some "overseas sources" mention the new OLED iPad mini has 120Hz specs, but that "domestic production volume has been confirmed" to use a 60Hz display.

I remain highly sceptical of this rumour, as no other reliable sources have yet corroborated it.

That said, if true, this would be a disappointing limitation for iPad mini buyers. The expected iPad mini upgrade this time is anticipated to bring a number of other notable improvements, including:

  • An OLED display.
  • The Apple A20 Pro chip, an upgrade over the current iPad mini's A17 Pro chip.
  • A redesigned exterior with thinner bezels and possibly improved water resistance.
  • The FaceTime camera will move to the landscape edge, in line with Apple's other iPad models.

If Apple makes all of the above changes but fails to upgrade the display to support ProMotion with a 120Hz refresh rate, it would significantly dent the appeal of the new iPad mini when it launches.

The new iPad mini is expected to launch later this month, so we won't have to wait long to find out the answer.

What do you think? Will the new iPad mini feature ProMotion and a 120Hz refresh rate? Let us know in the comments section.
